title: Unified Patient Read API for RapidChart and the ED tracker
subtitle: Read-only assemble of demographics, allergies, meds, and encounters from ChartLine, MedHarbor, and SiteNotes. Not a fourth EMR.
author: Aman Kumar
team: Clinical Integration / Patient API (Northstar at Riverview Health Network)
audience: Dr. Anita Shah (CMIO liaison), RapidChart and ED tracker leads, Luis Ortega (interfaces), Sneha Iyer (QA), Kavya Menon (backend), Chris Patel (data), Rahul Deshmukh (PM), incoming EM Priya Nair
owners: Aman Kumar (eng), Dr. Anita Shah (clinical), Kavya Menon (service), Luis Ortega (feeds), Sneha Iyer (QA)
related: RVH-2109 (driving ticket), RVH-2114 (allergy NKA merge), IFC-2020-CL-SOAP (Luis catalog), planned RVH-TDD-2021-004 (identity merge), planned FHIR-vs-REST TDD
summary: Clinical staff at Riverview's eleven facilities bounce between ChartLine, MedHarbor, and SiteNotes. This PRD specifies a unified read API for demographics, allergies, medications, and encounters so RapidChart (nursing) and the ED tracker can assemble a chart without becoming a write-back EMR. Identity stays per-facility MRN in v0. p95 assemble must stay under 1.8s on the campus network. Tableau on the warehouse was rejected; imaging binaries and billing are out of scope.
form_description: Product requirements for the Riverview unified patient read API, written for CMIO, nursing, integration, and Northstar engineering before the RapidChart Flagstaff pilot.
revision_history: Draft from RVH-2109 and the June CMIO rounding notes.
SLA from Flagstaff timing run. Cut write-back. Killed Tableau-on-warehouse after Patel/Shah review.
Approved for RapidChart and ED tracker kickoff. SiteNotes timeout window documented.

blocks.text: 1. Decision for leadership

Riverview Health Network runs eleven facilities on three source EMRs that do not share a patient identifier. Nursing and ED staff currently bounce between ChartLine (six campuses), MedHarbor (four campuses), and SiteNotes (Payson, acquired 2018). Ticket RVH-2109, opened by Dr. Anita Shah after the June 2020 CMIO rounding, asked Northstar to stop treating that bounce as a training problem. It is a data problem. This PRD covers a unified read API for demographics, allergies, medications, and encounters. First consumers are RapidChart (nursing documentation) and the ED tracker. We will not build a write-back EMR. We will not put Tableau on the warehouse and call it a chart.

Ask: approve scope, the 1.8s p95 assemble SLA on campus network, and the hard non-goal that this service never accepts clinical writes. Engineering owner is Aman Kumar. Clinical owner is Dr. Anita Shah. Feed owner is Luis Ortega. QA owner is Sneha Iyer. Chris Patel owns the warehouse path we are explicitly not using for online chart assemble. Kavya Menon owns the FastAPI service. Priya Nair joins as engineering manager in January 2021; until then I escalate product calls to Rahul Deshmukh and technical calls to Kavya.

blocks.label: Decision requested
blocks.text: Approve a read-only Patient Chart API (v0) serving RapidChart and the ED tracker from ChartLine, MedHarbor, and SiteNotes. Reject write-back, imaging binaries, billing, and a Tableau-on-warehouse substitute. Identity remains per-facility MRN in v0, with a merge service scheduled for Q1 2021. p95 chart assemble must stay under 1.8s on the campus VLAN (measured at Flagstaff RapidChart kiosk VLAN 214).

Why this is worth doing now: Flagstaff nursing already spends 4.7 minutes average per arrival flipping ChartLine then MedHarbor when a transfer comes from Phoenix Central. Denise Howell, nurse manager at Flagstaff, timed 38 arrivals in the week of August 3. Median was 3.9 minutes. Two cases exceeded 11 minutes because SiteNotes at Payson was on a Citrix jump. RapidChart cannot ship its nursing flow if the chart is still three logins. The ED tracker cannot color a bed if encounter state lives in three schemas. Shah's office will not sign a second documentation tool that writes back into ChartLine. That last sentence is the whole product constraint. We assemble a chart. We do not become the system of record.
2. Problem

Each facility issues its own MRN. Phoenix Central MRN 10488231 is a different person from Flagstaff MRN 10488231. The 2014 ChartLine conversion reused a block of six-digit MRNs at Cottonwood and Show Low. Luis Ortega has a spreadsheet, not a service, that tries to keep a crosswalk. The spreadsheet is named `mrn_xwalk_v17_FINAL_use_this.xlsx` on `fs-int-02.phx.riverview.internal` and it was last saved by Luis on May 11, 2020. Sneha pulled a copy for QA on August 6 and found 1,204 blank rows and 88 rows where last name plus DOB collided. Twins at Mesa Ridge are in there as one row. We will not pretend that file is identity.

Clinical staff do not talk about identity. They talk about the chart being wrong or slow. RapidChart's prototype, which Kavya demoed on August 14 in the Flagstaff basement conference room, called ChartLine's SOAP `GetPatient` (12.4s p95 from Phoenix, 1.1s p95 on campus), then MedHarbor's REST `/adt/v2/patients` (2.8s p95, 401s if the token clock is off by more than 47 seconds), then SiteNotes' HL7 query over a VPN that drops at 02:10 local when Payson's firewall restarts. The prototype did the three calls in series. That is why the room groaned. Parallel fan-out is a requirement, not a nice-to-have.

Allergies are the sharp edge. ChartLine stores `NO_KNOWN_ALLERGIES` as a coded row. MedHarbor stores an empty list and a separate boolean `nkaFlag`. SiteNotes stores the string `NKDA` on the encounter, not the patient. If we union those naively we drop the ChartLine row and RapidChart paints a blank allergy panel. Denise Howell said a blank panel is treated as "we did not look," which is worse than a documented NKA. Sneha already opened RVH-2114 for that merge rule. It belongs in this API, not in each consumer.

Medications have a different mess. ChartLine meds are inpatient MAR plus a home-meds free text blob. MedHarbor has RxNorm codes on 61.3% of active meds; the rest are local strings. SiteNotes at Payson still types drugs as `LISINOPRIL 10` without a code. The API will return source-tagged meds and a best-effort RxNorm when present. We will not invent a code. Chris Patel offered to map strings in the warehouse overnight. That map would be 18 hours stale and RapidChart cannot wait. Offline mapping is a later job, not v0.
If I have to open ChartLine to trust what RapidChart shows, RapidChart is a poster, not a chart. Do not give me a poster.
blocks.attrib: Denise Howell, Flagstaff nursing, August 14 2020 working session

blocks.text: 2.1 Who feels this

RapidChart is a nursing documentation client Northstar is building under a separate SOW. First unit is Flagstaff med-surg, then Phoenix Central ED overflow. The ED tracker is an existing Angular app on `ed-tracker.riverview.internal` that currently reads a MedHarbor-only feed and shows a gray bed for anyone whose encounter started in ChartLine. That is most transfers. Dr. Anita Shah's office owns clinical acceptance. Luis Ortega owns the three interface engines: `chartline-hl7.phx.riverview.internal`, `medharbor-rhapsody.tucson.riverview.internal`, `sitenotes-soap.mesa.riverview.internal`. Diego Alvarez will take the on-call once this has a pager, which it does not yet.

items: Nursing (RapidChart): needs one assemble call for demo, allergies, meds, open encounters. Will not write vitals through this API.
ED charge (ED tracker): needs encounter list by unit plus a patient header. Refresh every 15s. Stale data is visible as a timestamp, not hidden.
CMIO (Shah): needs an audit trail of who assembled whose chart, including break-glass. Will not accept a warehouse dashboard as a substitute.
Integration (Luis): needs a contract that does not require a fourth interface engine. Reads from the three we have.
QA (Sneha): needs fixtures with no real PHI. Golden files live in `git.riverview.internal/northstar/patient-api-fixtures`.

blocks.text: 3. Goals and non-goals
3.1 Goals for v0 (target: RapidChart Flagstaff pilot, December 14 2020)

items: GET assemble of demographics, allergies, medications, and encounters for a patient identified by (facility_id, local_mrn).
Fan-out to ChartLine, MedHarbor, and SiteNotes in parallel. Partial results allowed with a per-source status block.
p95 assemble under 1.8s on campus network (Flagstaff VLAN 214, Phoenix VLAN 108, Tucson VLAN 331). p99 under 3.4s. Timeout a single source at 1.2s and return the others.
Allergy merge that preserves NKA / NKDA / empty-list-with-flag as a first-class `allergy_status` so RapidChart never paints a blank panel when a source said none.
Audit every assemble: actor, patient keys, sources contacted, break-glass flag, duration_ms. Logs strip names and DOB. Correlation id only in application logs.
Contract tests against recorded ChartLine / MedHarbor / SiteNotes fixtures. No PHI in CI. Sneha owns the golden files.

blocks.text: 3.2 Non-goals (say no out loud)

items: Write-back of allergies, meds, problems, notes, or ADT. If RapidChart needs to document, it writes to ChartLine through the existing nursing flow, not through us.
Imaging binaries (PACS, PDF packets, scanned cards). Links to the existing viewer are out of band. Chris measured median CXR object at 18.6MB. We will not proxy that.
Billing, claims, coverage, or eligibility. Different system, different audit, different people.
A golden enterprise patient id in v0. Merge is a Q1 2021 design (see planned RVH-TDD-2021-004). v0 returns `local_ids[]` and `possible_matches[]` as hints only.
Tableau, PowerBI, or CensusMart as the online store. Warehouse freshness is 6.4h typical, 22h when the SiteNotes file drop misses the 01:15 job.
FHIR R4 as the public surface in v0. Internal debate is open (Kavya wants it, Shah does not want to wait for profile agreement). Tracked separately.

blocks.label: Rejected: Tableau on the warehouse
blocks.text: Chris Patel proposed pointing RapidChart at CensusMart (`censusmart.edw.riverview.internal`, nightly build `fact_inpatient_census`) and letting nursing 'filter to the patient.' That died in the August 21 review for four reasons. Grain is facility-day, not patient-encounter, so an ED stay that started at 23:40 does not exist until the next load. Freshness is 6.4 hours on a good night; Shah will not show that in an ED. Row-level access in Tableau Server is AD group by campus, not break-glass with a 15-minute reason code. And Tableau cannot serve RapidChart's assemble contract. We still want Chris's warehouse for retrospective census and quality. We will not use it as a chart.
4. Users, systems, and first consumers

Two paying consumers in v0. RapidChart talks to us from nursing workstations on the campus VLAN, mostly Chrome 84 on Windows 10 images named `W10-NURS-*`. The ED tracker talks to us from `ed-tracker-web-03.phx.riverview.internal` and from workstations at Flagstaff ED. Both will use service accounts in `rvh-svc-rapidchart` and `rvh-svc-edtracker` plus the human's badge assertion passed as `X-Actor-ID`. We log the human, not the service account, as the assembler. Diego asked that we not invent a fourth SSO. We will consume the existing SAML assertion Riverview already uses for ChartLine. Kavya has a spike in `patient-api/spikes/saml-actor` that parsed 200 sample assertions; 14 were missing `employeeNumber`. Those 14 cannot break-glass until IAM fills the attribute. Owner: Luis to open a ticket with IAM, not us.

blocks.caption: First consumers. No third consumer until assemble p95 holds for two weeks at Flagstaff.

blocks.text: Denise Howell will be the Flagstaff nursing sign-off. She is not a product owner. She is the person who will say the bed board is fiction if we get census wrong, which is why encounter uniqueness belongs in this API even though a full identity merge does not. For v0, uniqueness is (facility_id, local_mrn, encounter_id) inside one source. Cross-source duplicates are displayed as `possible_matches` with a score we will not auto-merge. Shah agreed that over-merge is worse than a nurse seeing two cards for one human. Under-merge means extra clicks. Over-merge means the wrong allergies. We pick extra clicks.
5. Identity in v0 (messy on purpose)

Every request keys a patient as `facility_id` plus `local_mrn`. Facility codes follow Luis's interface catalog, not the marketing names: `FLG`, `PHX-C`, `TUS-S`, `MESA`, `PRSC`, `YUMA`, `CWD`, `SHLO`, `KNG`, `SVIS`, `PAY`. Payson is SiteNotes-only. Flagstaff is ChartLine plus a MedHarbor ambulatory remnant for the 2019 clinic buy. A Flagstaff inpatient can have a ChartLine MRN and a leftover MedHarbor MRN from the clinic. RapidChart will pass both if nursing scanned both wristbands. We return one assemble document with `local_ids` listing both, and we do not pick a survivor. Picking a survivor is Q1 2021 work. If you auto-merge on last name + DOB + sex you will weld twins and you will weld the Cottonwood reused MRNs from the 2014 conversion. Do not do that in this service.

Possible matches: if ChartLine last+DOB+sex hits a MedHarbor person at a different facility, we attach `possible_matches[]` with score, source, and the fields that hit. Score is a stub in v0 (0.55 if last+DOB+sex, 0.00 otherwise). The real scorer belongs in identity-merge. RapidChart may show a yellow 'also seen at' chip. It may not combine allergy lists across a possible match. Sneha will write a test that fails the build if anyone unions allergies across unmatched ids.

blocks.text: 6. Functional requirements
6.1 Assemble

`GET /v0/patients/{facility_id}/{local_mrn}/assemble` returns a JSON document with `demographics`, `allergies`, `allergy_status`, `medications`, `encounters`, `sources[]`, `possible_matches[]`, `assembled_at`, `actor_id`. Optional query `sources=chartline,medharbor,sitenotes` to skip a known-down feed. Optional `encounter_id` to pin the header to one stay. RapidChart will call without `encounter_id` on arrival and with it once the bed is assigned. ED tracker always passes the unit's open encounters from its own cache, then calls header-only `GET /v0/patients/{facility_id}/{local_mrn}/header` which is demographics plus encounter state, no meds. Header p95 budget is 420ms. Assemble budget is 1.8s. Do not load meds on the 15s ED refresh. Kavya already saw a volunteer intern do that in the prototype. It melted ChartLine `GetPatient` at 09:12 on August 18. Luis got the page. We will rate-limit assemble to 2 req/s per actor and header to 8 req/s per service account.
Response rules that people will fight about

items: If all three sources 504, return 503 with `sources[].status=timeout`. Do not return a 200 with empty demographics. RapidChart must show failure, not a blank person.

If one source 504 and another 200, return 200 with partial flag `complete=false`. Include the failed source in `sources[]`. Denise would rather see ChartLine allergies plus a yellow 'MedHarbor timed out' than wait.
If the MRN is unknown in all sources, return 404. Do not return a stub person. ED tracker will keep the bed gray.

If IAM says the actor cannot see the facility, return 403. If the actor can see the facility but the chart is marked restricted (employee, VIP), return 401 until break-glass header `X-Break-Glass: reason` is present. Sneha caught the prototype mixing 401 and 403. Pick this mapping and do not drift. Restricted chart without glass is 401 (not authenticated for this chart). Wrong facility is 403 (authenticated, forbidden).

Break-glass lasts 15 minutes, is logged, and is not a role. It is a per-request header plus a server-side grant in Redis keyed by actor+patient for 15m. Redis host `redis-phi-01.flagstaff.riverview.internal`. PHI keys are hashes, not MRNs in the clear. Diego owns Redis capacity; we own the key layout.

blocks.text: 6.2 Demographics

Fields: legal name, preferred name if ChartLine has it (MedHarbor does not), DOB, sex as source-coded plus a mapped `sex_norm` of F/M/U/X, language, deceased flag, local ids. We do not return SSN, last-4, or mother's maiden on this API. Those fields may exist in ChartLine and may feed identity-merge later. They are not a RapidChart field. Shah was explicit. If a consumer needs them for matching, that consumer is the merge service, and it will talk to a different endpoint on a different port with a different audit. Do not sneak last-4 onto assemble because it would help the yellow chip. It would also land us in a privacy review we have not started.
6.3 Allergies and medications

Allergies return as a list of `{substance, reaction, severity, status, source, source_code, noted_at}` plus `allergy_status` of `documented_none`, `documented_list`, `unknown`. `documented_none` wins over empty. If ChartLine says NKA and MedHarbor returns an empty list, status is `documented_none` and the list is empty. If any source has an active allergy, status is `documented_list` and NKA rows are dropped (they contradict). If every source is unknown or timed out, status is `unknown` and RapidChart shows the warning panel, not a blank. Meds return `{name, rxnorm, dose, route, frequency, status, source, as_of}`. `status` is active/held/stopped as the source said. We do not compute a system-wide active set across sources in v0. RapidChart will group by source tab. Ugly. Clear.
6.4 Encounters

List of `{encounter_id, facility_id, source, class, unit, bed, admit_at, discharge_at, status}`. Timezone is America/Phoenix for every Riverview campus, including Flagstaff. Flagstaff follows Arizona, which does not observe DST. A contractor on the ED tracker already stored Flagstaff discharge as America/Denver. That will show a 1-hour slip from March to November. Sneha will add a fixture that fails if any timestamp is emitted without an offset. Storage is timestamptz. API emits RFC3339 with offset `-07:00`. Never emit Z for a Flagstaff discharge. Pagination: `GET /v0/patients/.../encounters?limit=&cursor=`. Default limit 50, max 200. Some ChartLine patients have 12.4k encounters (Mesa Ridge dialysis). Offset pagination dies at page 80. Cursor is `(admit_at, encounter_id)`. We will not offer `page=200`.
7. SLA and latency budget

Measured from the RapidChart kiosk on Flagstaff VLAN 214 to `api-patient-01.flagstaff.riverview.internal`, mid-shift, August 19-20, n=1,842 assemble calls against ChartLine only (the prototype). p50 640ms, p95 1.62s, p99 2.9s. Adding MedHarbor and SiteNotes in parallel is the risk. Budget below is what we will hold as an error budget, not a hope. If ChartLine p95 alone exceeds 1.4s we miss the assemble SLA even with parallel IO. Luis is talking to ChartLine hosting about the SOAP pool. That is not our ticket, but it is our SLA. We will expose `sources[].duration_ms` so RapidChart can show which source burned the budget.

blocks.caption: Latency budget for campus callers. Off-campus (VPN home) is best-effort and not in the SLA.

blocks.text: Availability target is 99.5% for assemble on weekdays 06:00-22:00 Arizona time, measured at the load balancer `lb-patient.riverview.internal`. That is about 3.6 hours a month, which sounds loose until you notice ChartLine SOAP already takes 1.1 hours a month in planned bounce. We will not claim three nines. Overnight we already know Payson dies at 02:10. ED tracker must tolerate `sources.sitenotes=down`. Diego wants a blackbox probe from Flagstaff and from Phoenix every 60s hitting a synthetic MRN that Luis created in each EMR (`MRN-SYNTH-00001` and friends). Probe traffic is excluded from RapidChart rate limits. Probe MRNs must never appear on a bed board. Filter `local_mrn LIKE 'MRN-SYNTH-%'`.
8. Security, PHI, and audit

Assemble bodies are PHI. They do not go to CI, to laptops, to Grafana, or to the warehouse topic Chris uses for CensusMart. Application logs may hold `correlation_id`, `actor_id`, hashed patient key, `facility_id`, `duration_ms`, source statuses. They may not hold names, DOB, addresses, meds, or allergy substances. Sneha will grep the log fixtures. Diego will drop a Promtail rule that fires if a log line matches a DOB regex. Break-glass reasons are free text; we will still store them because compliance asked. Max 200 chars. We will not put the reason on a dashboard. Audit rows land in Postgres `chart_audit.assemble_log` on `pg-patient-01.flagstaff.riverview.internal`, retained 7 years per Riverview policy RVH-PRIV-2018-04. That database is in the PHI VLAN. It is not the same Postgres as CensusMart.

Network: the API listens on campus only. Public DNS does not exist. Cert is the internal Riverview CA. RapidChart workstations already trust it. If someone publishes a route through the DMZ I will revert it. Luis confirmed the three source endpoints are reachable from the Flagstaff app VLAN and from Phoenix app VLAN. Tucson app VLAN can reach MedHarbor but hairpins ChartLine through Phoenix, which is why Tucson assemble may miss p95. We document that. We do not move ChartLine. Workaround is a Flagstaff sidecar for ChartLine SOAP with a 2s cache of demographics only, keyed by hash, TTL 45s. Allergies and meds are not cached. Encounters header can cache 15s to match ED tracker refresh. Cache is in Redis PHI. Empty 404s are not cached (Luis sometimes creates the MRN 20s after first scan).

blocks.label: PHI
blocks.text: No real patient payloads in git, CI, Slack, or email. Fixtures are synthetic, generated from Sneha's faker rules, and reviewed by Shah's office once. If a developer pastes an assemble body into a ticket, we delete the ticket comment and rotate the example. This is not theater. ChartLine SOAP responses include SSN when the calling cert has the 'full extract' right. Our cert must not have that right. Luis will request a cert with demographics-minus-SSN. If ChartLine cannot mint that cert, we strip SSN in the adapter and never persist it. Identity-merge can ask for a tokenized last-4 later, under a separate privacy review.
9. Service shape an engineer can build

Python 3.8, FastAPI, gunicorn+uvicorn workers, deployed as `patient-api` on two VMs: `api-patient-01.flagstaff.riverview.internal` and `api-patient-02.phx.riverview.internal`. No Kubernetes in this network yet. Systemd unit `patient-api.service`. Config in `/etc/patient-api/app.env` owned by root, read by `patient-api` user. Secrets in that file, not in git. Kavya's skeleton already speaks ChartLine SOAP via `zeep` and MedHarbor REST via `httpx`. SiteNotes is a thin MLLP client Luis wrote in 2019; we will vendor that module and not rewrite it. Postgres 12 for audit and for a small `id_hint` table that stores possible-match stubs. Redis 6 for break-glass grants and header cache.

blocks.text: Adapter timeouts live in config, not in code: `CHARTLINE_TIMEOUT_MS=1200`, `MEDHARBOR_TIMEOUT_MS=1200`, `SITENOTES_TIMEOUT_MS=900`. Circuit breaker: after 8 consecutive timeouts on a source, open for 30s, then half-open on one probe. Prometheus metrics: `patient_api_assemble_ms`, `patient_api_source_ms{source=}`, `patient_api_source_timeouts{source=}`, `patient_api_partial_total`, `patient_api_breakglass_total`. Alert if p95 assemble > 1.8s for 10 minutes on Flagstaff. Alert if ChartLine timeout ratio > 8.2% for 5 minutes. Do not alert on Payson at 02:10-02:25. That is the firewall restart. Put a silence on SiteNotes for that window or we will page Diego every night and he will disable the alert.
Postgres objects (audit + hints only)

-- pg-patient-01.flagstaff.riverview.internal, database patient_api
CREATE TABLE chart_audit.assemble_log (
  id              bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  assembled_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  correlation_id  uuid NOT NULL,
  actor_id        text NOT NULL,
  facility_id     text NOT NULL,
  patient_key     text NOT NULL, -- hmac of facility||mrn, not the mrn
  break_glass     boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  complete        boolean NOT NULL,
  duration_ms     integer NOT NULL,
  sources         jsonb NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX assemble_log_at_ix ON chart_audit.assemble_log (assembled_at);
CREATE INDEX assemble_log_actor_ix ON chart_audit.assemble_log (actor_id, assembled_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE id_hint.possible_match (
  id              bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  left_key        text NOT NULL,
  right_key       text NOT NULL,
  score           numeric(4,3) NOT NULL,
  rule            text NOT NULL,
  created_at      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (left_key, right_key, rule)
);
-- v0 writer is a stub. Real scorer is identity-merge in 2021.
blocks.caption: Audit is the only PHI-adjacent store in v0. possible_match holds keys, not names.

blocks.text: 10. Error catalog and failure modes
This is the section to keep open while writing adapters. Partial success is a first-class outcome. Most of our pain will be 'one of three sources is lying' rather than the API process being down.

blocks.caption: Failure modes for v0. Audit-down does not block assemble. ChartLine-down does not block MedHarbor data.

blocks.text: Over-cache failure: if we ever cache allergies for 45s and ChartLine posts a new penicillin row at second 10, RapidChart can show NKA until second 45. That is why allergies are not in the 45s cache. Only demographics (name, DOB, sex) and encounter header (unit, bed, status). If someone adds allergies to that Redis blob in a 'performance' PR, reject it. I will reject it. Shah will reject it louder.

Clock failure: MedHarbor signs tokens with the Tucson AD clock. On August 11 that clock was 51 seconds ahead after a failed NTP step. Every RapidChart call 401'd for 18 minutes. Adapter must treat source 401 as `sources.medharbor=auth` and still return ChartLine data. RapidChart shows a banner. It does not blank the page. Kavya will add a `/internal/source-health` that reports token age and last SOAP success. Not public.
11. Analytics we are not building

Rahul asked whether assemble events could feed a 'chart completeness' dashboard. Not in v0. Completeness is a clinical definition Shah has not written. We can count `complete=false` and source timeouts. We cannot score whether the allergy list is clinically enough. Chris can land timeout rates in CensusMart later from the audit table's non-PHI columns (facility, duration, source status). That extract is a batch, not a pipeline off the hot path. No Kafka in this environment yet. Nightly `COPY` to the EDW jump is fine. Do not subscribe Tableau to `assemble_log`. The table has hashed keys and actor ids; still too close.
12. Rollout

items: Week of Aug 31: freeze this PRD. Kavya splits adapter work. Luis orders ChartLine cert without SSN. Sneha starts fixture recorder against ChartLine CERT, not PROD.
Week of Sep 14: parallel fan-out behind a feature flag on Flagstaff only. Synthetic MRNs only. Diego adds blackbox probe.
Week of Oct 5: Shah and Denise sit with RapidChart on 12 synthetic scenarios including NKA, restricted chart, Payson down, MedHarbor 401.
Week of Nov 2: limited real Flagstaff med-surg users, 2 nurses per shift, paper ChartLine still primary. Assemble SLA watched live.
Dec 14: RapidChart Flagstaff pilot if p95 < 1.8s for 10 consecutive days and zero SSN-in-log events. ED tracker stays flagged off until January.
Jan 2021: Priya Nair takes engineering management. Identity-merge design starts. ED tracker flag for Phoenix ED.

blocks.text: Rollback is turning the RapidChart feature flag off. The API can stay up for probes. We do not have dual-write because we do not write. That is the one gift of the non-goal. If ChartLine SOAP is the problem, RapidChart goes back to opening ChartLine. Denise would rather that than a wrong allergy panel.

blocks.text: 14. What success looks like in December

A Flagstaff med-surg nurse on RapidChart scans a wristband, sees name, allergies with a real `documented_none` or a list, meds from ChartLine, and the current encounter bed, in under 1.8 seconds on a normal shift, without opening ChartLine for the common case. When MedHarbor is drunk, she still sees ChartLine data and a yellow source chip. When the chart is restricted, she is asked for a reason and the reason is logged. When Payson VPN is down, Payson patients show partial and nobody pages Diego at 02:12. Tableau is still used by quality for last night's census, which is the job it has. RapidChart is not a poster. This PRD is the contract that keeps us from turning a read API into a fourth EMR because someone asked for a write 'just for allergies.' The answer to that request is no. File a different ticket.

Ticket still driving this work: RVH-2109. Related: RVH-2114 (allergy NKA merge), Luis catalog `IFC-2020-CL-SOAP`, planned identity design Q1 2021, planned FHIR-vs-REST TDD if Shah wants a second surface. I will keep this document at v1.2 until RapidChart pilot. If the SLA moves, the number in section 7 moves first and this summary moves second. Do not bury a quieter SLA in an adapter config and leave 1.8s on the cover.
